pool.text: Named after Adelaide of Saxe-Meiningen, the city was founded as a planned British colony.
The Holy Trinity Church on North Terrace was built as the first church.
Governor Hindmarsh created the South Australian Police Force under Henry Inman.
Adelaide's early economy started to get on its feet with livestock arrivals.
The Royal Adelaide Show was established as an annual agricultural show.
James Hurtle Fisher was elected as Australia's first mayor.
Kaurna culture was almost completely lost with the last speaker passing away.
The Adelaide Electric Supply Company was nationalised by the Playford government to become ETSA.
Adelaide Airport opened, replacing Parafield Airport as the city's main aerodrome.
The Mannum–Adelaide pipeline brought River Murray water to the city.
The biennial Adelaide Festival of Arts commenced to anchor the arts scene.
South Australia became the first Australian state to decriminalise homosexuality.
Massada College, a Jewish day school, opened in the city.
Premier David Tonkin committed his government to selling off MATS plan land.
The State Bank collapsed during an economic recession.
The collapse of the State Bank resulted in large levels of state debt.
The Olsen Government privatised ETSA through a lease and outright purchase arrangement.
The Adelaide Festival of Ideas was established as a separate festival.
A decision was made to revert the ship's name to the City of Adelaide.
It was officially launched at the Adelaide Central Markets.
